items.followUp: Define a polyatomic ion and give one example.

rubric.why: Checks the defining features of a molecular ion.
rubric.description: Defines a molecular ion as a group of bonded atoms carrying a net charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for identifying both the group of atoms and its charge.

rubric.why: Checks the difference in overall electrical charge.
rubric.description: States that a molecule is neutral whereas a molecular ion is charged.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for clearly contrasting the charge of each.

rubric.why: Checks the difference in proton and electron numbers.
rubric.description: States that a molecule has equal numbers of protons and electrons, while a molecular ion has unequal numbers.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for stating both sides of the comparison.

rubric.why: Checks how molecules and molecular ions are represented.
rubric.description: Shows a molecule written without a charge and a molecular ion written with its charge.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for a correct paired example with the ion's charge shown.

rubric.why: Checks the different behaviour of neutral and charged particles in an electric field.
rubric.description: States that a molecule is not deflected, whereas a molecular ion is deflected in an electric field.
rubric.how: Award 1 mark for contrasting the behaviour of both in an electric field.

modelAnswer: A molecular ion is a group of two or more covalently bonded atoms that carries a net positive or negative charge and behaves as a single ion.
A molecule is electrically neutral, whereas a molecular ion carries a net charge.
A molecule has the same number of protons and electrons; a molecular ion has unequal numbers of protons and electrons.
A molecule is written without a charge, for example H₂O; a molecular ion is written with its charge, for example NH₄⁺.
A molecule is not deflected by an electric field, whereas a molecular ion is deflected by it.
